title: Netherlands – Marine survey services – Raamovereenkomst Vooronderzoeken Baggeren Lansingerland
description: Baggerwerkzaamheden maken onderdeel uit van het reguliere beheer en onderhoud van de watergangen binnen de gemeente Lansingerland en vormen daarmee een periodiek terugkerende activiteit. Om de benodigde baggerwerkzaamheden planmatig en doelmatig te kunnen voorbereiden, dient periodiek te worden vastgesteld welke watergangen in aanmerking komen voor uitvoering in de daaropvolgende jaren. De gemeente is voornemens een raamovereenkomst af te sluiten voor het uitvoeren van de benodigde vooronderzoeken en toezicht op baggeren. Deze vooronderzoeken omvatten onder meer het bepalen van het te baggeren areaal, het uitvoeren van waterbodem- en ecologische onderzoeken en overige onderzoeken die noodzakelijk zijn voor de voorbereiding van baggerwerken. De resultaten van deze onderzoeken vormen de basis voor het samenstellen van uitvoerbare werkpakketten voor de reeds gecontracteerde baggeraar. De verwachte omzet voor vier jaar bedraagt € 380.000,-. Het Plafondbedrag van de raamovereenkomst voor vier jaar bedraagt € 494.000,-.

title: Firefox
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) has developed a non-invasive coherent optical system capable of recording neural signals in humans. To expand this foundational technology and enable the development of revolutionary, non-invasive brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), DARPA's Firefox program is soliciting approaches to overcome key technological hurdles: 1) development of components enabling dynamic rastering/scanning of the incoming coherent optical signal to target multiple regions of interest and 2) development of new data processing architectures beyond the digital domain to handle the high data rates and computational burden inherent to scaling the amount of neural data recorded by the optical system. The ultimate goal of the Firefox program is to use these innovations to develop a 100-channel, non-invasive BCI with 50-micron spatial and 100-microsecond temporal resolution.

title: Solicitation - BWT Operation and Maintenance
description: SOLICITATION - OPERATIONS AND MAINTENANCE OF GOVERNMENT-OWNED FACILITIES AND EQUIPMENT, BLACK WARRIOR- TOMBIGBEE AND ALABAMA RIVER WATERWAYS PROJECT FACILITIES, ALABAMA - Furnish all planning, supervision, administration, labor, equipment, material, supplies, replacement or repair parts, and all things necessary for the Operations and Maintenance of Government-Owned Facilities and Equipment, Black Warrior- Tombigbee and Alabama River Waterways Project Facilities, Alabama. The project is geographically spread out over 13 counties in Alabama: Washington, Clarke, Marengo, Choctaw, Sumter, Hale, Greene, Tuscaloosa, Monroe, Wilcox, Dallas, Lowndes, and Autauga Counties, on the Black Warrior and Tombigbee BWT River System and the Alabama River System. The Project Management Office has responsibility for the operation and maintenance of nine locks and dams, two resource offices, a Project Management Office, two boat houses, one boat storage facility, storage buildings, two contractor maintenance compounds, and two hydro-electric generating plants. The BWT/AL Project is home to 9 beautiful lakes, they include Bankhead, Holt, Oliver, Warrior, Demopolis, Coffeeville, Claiborne, Millers, and RF Henry. These lakes for the BWT stretch from the headwaters near Birmingham, AL, south through Tuscaloosa and Demopolis to the southernmost Mobile District Corps facility located below Coffeeville, and for the AL river south from Montgomery, AL to the confluence with the Tombigbee River. The project is operated under the direction of Mobile District, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Mobile, Alabama. It is anticipated that one 1 Firm-Fixed Price FFP, Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity IDIQ, Single Award Task Order Contract SATOC will be awarded for a five 5-year ordering period. In general, not all inclusive, services to be performed include general maintenance, cleaning, custodial service, garbage removal, grass mowing, saddle dike and overlook clearing, debris removal, clerical duties at a Resource Office, repair to riprap slopes, repair to earthen slopes, excavation, and storage and disposal of hazardous and-or toxic materials, such as herbicides and waste fluids from vehicle maintenance. The IDIQ performance work statement PWS will include, but is not limited to, the following types of work: maintenance and repair of locks, dams, levees, riprap-concrete structures, flow structures, buildings, offices, maintenance facilities, operation areas, project roads, vehicles, floating plant, boathouses, bathhouses, washhouses, toilets, gatehouses, security and other fences, sanitary disposal systems, small boat launching ramps, playground equipment, bulletin boards, game courts, water and electrical systems, telephone lines, picnic sites, campsites, and other related facilities. Tasks required to perform this type of maintenance include carpentry, masonry, electrical, electronics, mechanical, structural, plumbing, chipping, caulking, sealing, cleaning, welding and replacing parts of or full pieces of equipment. Additional maintenance work includes guardrails, gates, electric barrier gates, signs, bumper blocks, landscaped areas, beaches, navigation or swimming buoys, paved roads, parking lots, trails, navigation aids, courtesy docks, and boundary lines. Operational requirements encompass the maintenance of a specialized floating plant comprising a primary towboat, crane barge, and auxiliary workboats and barges to support the Black Warrior-Tombigbee BWT and Alabama River Systems. This area of responsibility AOR extends from the mouth of the Mobile River to Birmingham on the BWT system and to Montgomery on the Alabama River system. These multi-purpose civil works projects are vital to facilitating commercial navigation, supporting public recreation, and managing regional wildlife habitats. This procurement is 100% set-aside for small business. title: Laboratory Support Services
description: The Defense Prisoner of War/Missing in Action Accounting Agency (DPAA) conducts global research, investigation, recovery, and laboratory operations to identify and account for unaccounted-for Department of Defense (DoD) personnel from past conflicts. These efforts support the DoD personnel accounting mission. DPAA was established on January 30, 2015; however, its predecessor organizations have supported the personnel accounting mission for decades. DPAA operates a satellite laboratory at Offutt Air Force Base, Nebraska, which opened in June 2013. DPAA also maintains permanent detachments that support host-nation access, logistics, and in-country requirements for investigation and recovery operations. These detachments include Detachment 1 in Bangkok, Thailand; Detachment 2 in Hanoi, Vietnam; Detachment 3 in Vientiane, Laos; and Detachment Europe in Miesau, Germany. DPAA Scientific Analysis (SA), also referred to as the DPAA laboratory, is a large and diverse forensic skeletal laboratory staffed by forensic anthropologists, archaeologists, and odontologists. The laboratory performs scientific analysis to support the identification of missing personnel. In 2003, the laboratory became the second Federal laboratory to achieve accreditation under the American Society of Crime Laboratory Directors/Laboratory Accreditation Board (ASCLD/LAB) International Standards Program. Laboratory accreditation supports the DoD Defense Forensic Enterprise program and is consistent with DoD Directive 5110.10, Defense POW/MIA Accounting Agency (DPAA). DPAA regional directorates, including the Indo-Pacific (IP) Directorate and Europe-Mediterranean (EM) Directorate, conduct complex historical research and archaeological analysis in support of recovery, investigation, and disinterment missions. The regional directorates plan and execute field investigations and recovery operations worldwide. The Partnerships and Innovations Directorate supports these global field operations. This contract supports DPAA laboratory and regional-directorate requirements necessary to advance the Agency�s mission of accounting for as many missing service members as feasible each year. DPAA�s planning objective is to maintain the capacity and capability to account for 200 or more individuals annually.

description: Sources Sought Synopsis PROJECT TITLE: Kissimmee River Restoration (KRR) Project, S-69 Weir Repair This is announcement constitutes a Source Sought Synopsis and seeks information from industry which will only be used for preliminary planning purposes. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR BIDS AND NO CONTRACT SHALL BE AWARDED FROM THIS SYNOPSIS. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. The South Atlantic Jacksonville District of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (SAJ) is seeking interest from prospective bidders for a potential fiscal year (FY) 2027 contract award for the subject construction project. SAJ has a requirement for the repair of components of the existing S-69 weir structure inclusive of sheet pile�s concrete cap and ancillary concrete driving slab. The purpose of this sources sought is to gauge interest, capabilities, and qualifications of contractors that have experience in completing similar projects. The scope of the contract is inclusive of but not limited to (a) partial concrete cap demolition, (b) inspection and cleaning of existing concrete, steel bars, anchor studs and steel sheet piles, (c) preparation of studs and rebar, (d) installation of new closed-loop epoxy coated stirrups routed through the sheet pile and new anchor studs welded to the sheet pile, (e) provision of new expansion joints, (f) repairing of concrete caps with structural concrete, (g) driving slab subsurface void investigation and subsequent repairs to address separation of the slab from sheet pile, and (h) all quality control and construction administration submittals relevant to the construction effort, including as-builts of the final repaired structure. The proposed project will be a Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract. The Jacksonville District anticipates the issuance of a Request for Proposal (RFP). No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this Sources Sought or any follow-up information requested. DESCRIPTION OF WORK: The S-69 Weir consists of driven sheet pile walls with a concrete cap that acts as a weir and is a key feature of the Kissimmee River Restoration (KRR) Project. Located in Okeechobee and Highlands Counties, Florida, the weir�s primary function is to restore the Kissimmee River�s floodplain hydrology to pre-canal conditions by controlling water stages and discharges into the C-38 canal. Repair of components of the existing S-69 weir structure require sheet pile concrete cap and driving concrete slab. Anticipated work includes but is not limited to: concrete removal portions of the cap, addition of new reinforcement steel closed stirrups, welding of anchor studs, providing expansion joint material, casting-in-place new structural concrete, assessment of voids underneath the driving slab through concrete coring and grouting of cored holes, and filling of gaps between the slab and cap with Controlled Low Strength Material (CSLM) or equivalent approved flowable fill. The overall project site components encompass work to done at the following approximate location: 27.334767, -81.032830; very close to the �Chandler Slough South Trailhead�. Specific project components include the following items and incidental related work; refer to conceptual plans for further information: Concrete Cap Repair 1. Concrete Cap Partial Demolition at Expansion Joints a. At 29 expansion joint locations, demolish 36� of concrete cap on each side of expansion joint. Existing rebar and sheet pile studs to remain. 2. Inspection and Cleaning of Existing Concrete, Steel Bars, Anchor Studs, and Steel Sheet Piles prior to new repair. a. Use blast cleaning techniques for steel. Demolish concrete beyond the 36� footprint if concrete material is weak and unsuitable. 3. Drilling/Burning of holes into sheet pile to allow for closed stirrups to pass through. a. Drill or burn 2-inch diameter holes to allow installation of closed-hoop steel stirrups. 4. Welding of new anchor studs to sheet pile. a. Anchor stud size is 1/2"(diameter) x 4� 5. Preparation of Studs and Rebar (Coating) prior to new repair a. Apply inorganic zinc-based primer for all existing rebar as well as both existing and new studs (coating to be applied after welding). 6. Installation of new #5 closed-loop epoxy-coated stirrups at 6� on-center, with the bottom leg routed through the sheet pile. a. First stirrup must be 3� from expansion joint, all others to follow the spacing requirement. 7. Provision of new expansion joints. a. Expansion joint thickness must be increased to 2�. Use Class 50 system, with ASTM C920 elastomeric sealant rated for at least 50% movement an documented as suitable for the anticipated weather and ultraviolet exposures, temperature range, and substrate conditions. 8. Repair of concrete cap using structural cast-in-place concrete (f�c = 4,500 psi). a. Concrete quality, placement, consolidation, and curing procedures per plans and specifications will be strictly monitored by both Contractor QC and Government QA personnel. Ancillary North Driving Slab Repair 1. Coring layout and investigation of potential subsurface voids a. Core drill 20 cores into the slab from approximately STA 23+80 to 25+20 (centered about the primary area of concern near STA 24+50). Cores will be spaced at approximately 20-foot intervals and positions 2 to 5 feet from the inner wall to characterize conditions directly adjacent to the gap. Core drill new cores spaced at approximately 40-foot intervals along the remainder of the Northern leg. b. Investigate cored areas for voids underneath the slabs. Coordinate with the Government for any adverse conditions found. c. Fill all core holes with non-shrink grout after Government inspection. 2. Repair of separated slab at North leg of weir. a. The 3-inch separation as indicated in concept drawings and all other voids must be filled with Controlled Low Strength Material (CLSM) or an approved flowable fill. 3. Repair of slab�s expansion joints a. Expansion joints of the driving slab must be mechanically routed or scraped out, joint faces cleaned and prepared, new closed-cell backer rod installed to achieve the proper depth-to-width ration, and heavy-duty, UB-resistant elastomeric joint sealant applied. Construction Submittals and As-Builts 1. Providing quality control and all required submittals during construction, which includes but is not limited to, the void investigation report, concrete mix design, and all product data. 2. Providing as-built documentation once repair is completed. title: Comprehensive full-service maintenance/repair plan for Vitek 2 Compact 60
description: The United States Department of the Navy Medicine Research and Development Command (NMRDC) intends to award a sole source contract to, bioMerieux, Inc, Salt Lake City, UT 84108. This notice is not a request for competitive proposals however If interested Government shall consider all responses. The Genomics and Bioinformatics Department of the Biological Defense Research Directorate, NMRDC-Frederick maintains a state-of-the-art genomics and bioinformatics research program. As part of their ongoing efforts to diminish the burden that increased antimicrobial resistance pose for the health of our military, the Vitek 2 Compact system will be used to characterize the antibiotic resistance profiles of pathogenic bacteria isolated from clinically relevant enteric samples and compare those phenotypic data to the genes detected via sequencing. Without proper service agreements, mission critical scientific research may be compromised. This instrument is a delicate, specialized, highly technical, state-of-the-art laboratory instrument that must receive preventative maintenance and periodic updates in accordance with the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) standards/procedures by certified, authorized technicians, and be covered by a comprehensive maintenance/repair support plan/agreement in the case of hardware malfunction/failure. The need is for a Comprehensive full-service maintenance/repair plan for a Vitek 2 Compact 60. One year support plan must include at a minimum: Full coverage for OEM parts and labor/travel for OEM certified and authorized service technicians. One on-site preventative maintenance (PM) visit done IAW OEM standards/requirements by OEM certified and authorized service technician(s). Remote technical support from OEM certified and authorized service technician(s). This support is provided 24 hours a day / 7 days a week. On-site response by OEM certified and authorized service technician(s) within 24 hours of an issue with the hardware�s performance using commercially reasonable efforts. The NAICS code for this action is 811210. This requirement will be procured under the guidelines of FAR Part 12 Commercial Items. NMRDC requires that all contractors doing business with the Acquisition Office must be registered with the Systems for Award Management (SAM). No award can be made unless the vendor is registered in Systems for Award Management. For additional information and to register in SAM, please access the following website: https://www.sam.gov/. In order to register with the SAM and to be eligible to receive an award from this Acquisition Office, all offers must have a Unique Entity Identification Number (UEI). A Sam.gov number may be acquired free of charge by contacting Sam.gov online at www.sam.gov or by phone at (866) 606-8220.

Kilpailutuksen vertailuperuste ja tarjotut hinnat: 1. Määräaikaishuoltohinta, annetaan excel tarjouslomakkeiden avulla. 2. Korjaustyön tuntihinta, syötetään cloudiassa suoraan ilman exceliä. 3. Les travaux comprennent notamment : l’aménagement de locaux télécoms (baies, coffrets, têtes de câbles optiques, chemins de câbles, mise à la terre) ; l’aménagement des prises et tableaux de distribution d’énergie ; le déroulage, le raccordement et les tests de câbles courants faibles (cuivre, LAN, fibre optique) ; le déroulage et le raccordement de câbles courants forts alimentant les installations télécoms ; la pose d’équipements télécoms en gare et sur quai (écrans de téléaffichage, caméras, haut-parleurs, balises sonores, horloges, bornes wifi, antennes, supports et mâts) ; la pose de fourreaux et tubes PEHD, de câbles cuivre et de fibres optiques ; la confection de prises de terre et de terres longitudinales ; les travaux de petit génie civil associés (massifs, fourreaux, percements, bris de béton). Les détails sont précisés au DCE. Chaque lot est attribué à deux titulaires : le titulaire de rang 1 (mieux-disant) et le titulaire de rang 2 (second mieux-disant). Les bons de commande sont répartis en montant à hauteur de 70 % (± 10 %) pour le titulaire de rang 1 et de 30 % (± 10 %) pour le titulaire de rang 2, sur chaque période d’exécution. Cette répartition s’applique aux bons de commande effectivement émis et ne constitue pas un engagement de volume. Le montant de chaque bon de commande est plafonné à 200 000 € HT. L’accord-cadre comprend une tranche ferme de 2 ans, du 10/05/2027 au 09/05/2029, et une reconduction éventuelle d’un an, du 10/05/2029 au 09/05/2030. Les candidats peuvent candidater à un ou plusieurs lots. Un même soumissionnaire ne peut être attributaire de plus de 2 lots en rang 1 et de plus de 2 lots en rang 2, selon les règles précisées dans le règlement de consultation.

title: Synthetic Signature Generation (SSG) Support Services
description: The Department of the Navy, Naval Surface Warfare Center, Carderock Division (NSWCCD) is soliciting for scientific, engineering, and technical services required for the design, development, fabrication, integration, test, fleet implementation, and maintenance of Synthetic Signature Generation (SSG) based simulation systems. The Government requires support system installations and updates required for the following five categories of Navy fleet training systems: Submarine Team, Navigation, Surface, Surveillance, and On-Board. The Government requires design, development, integration, testing, delivery, installation, and maintenance of fielded systems. The Government requires technical engineering support for simulation and training system capabilities to existing fleet onsite maintenance personnel for the operational systems. The Government also requires support for tactical testing and analysis system configurations for common simulation and tactical subsystems utilized in these trainers. The Government is soliciting this requirement as full-and-open competition. The contract will be awarded as a single award indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity(IDIQ), with Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF) Level of Effort (LOE) CLINs and Cost Only Other Direct Costs (ODCs) CLINs for incidental materials and travel. The contract will be for a period of three years to include three one-year ordering periods.

title: 63100PR270000009 Repair Floating Dock
description: Contractor to provide all labor, materials, and equipment necessary to repair the floating Jet Docks, BLDG 292. Work consists of: Remove and replace 18 damaged large Module Assemblies (MAs). Remove and replace 40 open well style or damaged small MAs and replace with standard small MAs. Remove and replace keel deflection system (KDS) on all nine docks. Remove and replace all pontoon straps and hardware (36� lifting eyes) for all nine docks. Remove and replace all 27 structural support beams and all 18 pontoon guide beams across all nine docks � 45 total. Install new cathodic protection system on all beams � 45 total. Remove valves and wiring on powerhead for all nine docks and replace with standard valves and wires. Install two freshwater washdown hoses, 40 ft length, per dock � 18 total. Install protection system between MAs and piling � one per dock, nine total. Install bunk tusk system, one per dock, nine total. Rebuild the dock stern to include intermediate corrugation support on all nine docks. Remove and replace any damaged pontoons with the same size and kind. If no longer in production, replace with closest approximation � approximately 6 pontoons. Install additional MAs on docks that are assigned the 29 ft RB-S II boats � 5 docks total, approximately 30 large MAs, 5 small MAs. Install new inner bunk systems on all docks to accommodate the boats described below: 29 ft RB-S II boats (8,400 lbs), 26 ft TANB boats (7,300 lbs), and 26 ft CB-OTH-V boats (7,470 lbs). Calibrate existing and replacement pontoons for the boats described above. For a layout of dock assignments, refer to the included drawing 2-29202-1.

title: Sources Sought -Building 493 Generator and Backup Power Installation- Red River Army Depot
description: MARKET RESEARCH ONLY Title: Red River Army Depot Standby Generator Location: New Boston, Texas Scope: This project will install a 1300 KW Generator and two 500kw generators, a 3000 KVA step-up transformer, and 15 kV switchgear to provide backup power to Building 493. The equipment will provide a Distributed Infrastructure (DI) system within RRAD. The proposed system will provide 100% standby power and will be designed for closed transition operation with AEP/SWEPCO for Standby Response. Provide complete engineering, procurement, and construction of back-up generation facilities for RRAD buildings 493 (Rubber Operations), M495 (fluidized bed), and the compressor service supporting building 493. Back-up generation is intended to counter outages which cause significant downtime and cost impacts to the operation. Facilities will be designed to a minimum life of 40 years in accordance with DoD's Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC 1-200-02) including energy efficiencies, building envelope and integrated building systems performance. Target Price Range (TPR): The Government has established The Government's Target Price for construction is between $4,800,000 and $5,127,000 (the strict CCL) with a programmed PA of $5,700,000. title: Granite Surface Plate Calibration and lapping - with Q&As
description: Q&A's: 1. CLINs 0001 through 0005 (pages 3-5) are each one firm-fixed-price lot for "Inspection and calibration." SOW paragraphs 1 and 4.2 (pages 1-2) call for lapping only of plates that are out of specification, the QASP (Attachment 0002, page 1) says lapping repairs must be authorized by the CO or COR, and Section G, paragraph 6.a (page 12) asks for labor rates. Should each year's lot price cover inspection and calibration of all 18 plates, with lapping priced separately (for example, a per-plate price or an hourly labor rate) and billed only when authorized? Or should the lot price include all lapping that may be needed that year? If lapping is priced separately, where in the quote should those prices or rates be shown? Answer: Firm fixed for calibration of all plates listed in the SOW. Lapping to be priced separately. We don�t know which plates will require lapping or how much lapping per plate will be needed. We are asking for an hourly rate for lapping. Whether the plate is big or small, the hourly rate would be the same. Plates may require a lot of lapping or very little. Pricing lapping by the plate doesn�t seem to make much sense. 2. Each CLIN (pages 3-5) states "All travel shall be in accordance with the Joint Travel Regulation (JTR)," and SOW paragraph 2 (page 1) says invoices will be checked against the contract prices and JTR approved prices. Should travel be included in each year's firm-fixed lot price, or will it be reimbursed separately at JTR rates? If it is reimbursed separately, how should travel be shown in the quote? Answer: Include estimated travel costs in the firm-fixed pricing. The Vendor that gets the award will bill actual costs after the service. 3. Section G, paragraph 6.c (page 12) asks offerors to "concur at the bottom of the Scope of Work (SOW) and sign," but Attachment 0001 ends at paragraph 15.1 on page 4 with no concurrence or signature block. Is it acceptable to add a signed and dated concurrence statement at the bottom of SOW page 4, or to submit a separate signed concurrence page on company letterhead that references Attachment 0001 dated 15 Oct 26? Answer: Either is fine by me. _______________________ All Vendors MUST submit all requirements plus the signed Soliciation to the POC before the closing date and time or they will not be considered for this action.

description: 657-27-103JB, FCA Replace Building 51 Roof This is a Sources Sought Notice to determine the availability of service disabled veteran owned small business (SDVOSB) firms for a possible small business category type set-aside for Construction Services project: This is a Sources Sought Notice that is issued for information and planning purposes only and is not to be construed as a commitment� by the government, implied or otherwise to issue a solicitation or ultimately award a contract.� An award will not be made on information received in response to this notice.� This notice is not a Request for Proposal (RFP); it is a market research tool being utilized to determine the availability of sources prior to issuing a Best Value type RFP. PROJECT DESCRIPTION AND SCOPE 1. This contract is for CONSTRUCTION services for the work required to replace the existing roof and associated components on Building 51 at the St. Louis Medical Center Jefferson Barracks. 2. Description: Construction services: Furnish complete construction services to replace all designated Building 51 roofs, including projections, entrance roofs, and connecting portions. The preliminary net roof area is approximately 56,000 square feet, subject to field verification. Provide a watertight thermoplastic polyolefin (TPO) roofing system in accordance with the VA-prepared drawings and specifications. Contractor shall submit shop drawings, product data, and installation details for all proposed materials, equipment, and systems to be installed or replaced under this contract for VA review prior to commencing the associated work. Submittals shall include applicable manufacturer's specifications and required engineering certifications. Schedule, phasing, and occupied operations: Complete construction and closeout within 222 calendar days after the Notice to Proceed issue date. Building 51 remains occupied and operational 24 hours per day, seven days per week. Work hours are from 7:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., local time. Submit a contractor-developed phasing plan for the Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) to review before roofing. Complete both highest penthouse roof platforms first on the original building and the highest roof section first on the addition; either building portion may be started first. Maintain safe access, utilities, and required infection-control and HVAC-intake protection. Provide construction fall protection and keep the building watertight; coordinate service interruptions with the VA. Investigation and Roofing Requirements: a. Hazardous Materials: While neither Asbestos Containing Material nor Lead is expected to be encountered within the scope of this project, it will be the responsibility of the contractor to hire an independent 3rd party VPIH to complete the related work if they are to encounter a material that they deem suspicious. b. Demolition limit: At the original building (Zones 1-7, 13, and 14), remove the existing roofing assembly through the base sheet to the top of the Zonolite lightweight-concrete topping; retain the topping and underlying structural concrete deck. At the addition (Zones 8-12 and 15), remove the existing roofing assembly, including insulation and intervening layers, to the top of the metal roof deck; retain the deck and supporting structure. Clean and inspect retained surfaces, and repair deterioration within specified repair limits. Report differing construction or deterioration beyond those limits to the COR before proceeding with affected work. c. New roof and mechanical securement: Install mechanically fastened rigid insulation, adhered cover board, and fully adhered 70-mil TPO roofing membrane with continuous hot-airwelded seams. Contractor shall verify that the proposed fastening system is compatible with Building 51's existing roof construction. d. Parapets, penetrations, and retained metal: Extend new roofing up parapets to the existing flashing. Flash and seal, with the correct system specific boots, all roof penetrations with compatible membrane extending at least 8 inches above the finished roof, or higher where required by applicable VA criteria and manufacturer/warranty requirements. Retain metal flashings, flanges, and coping unless scheduled for replacement, and replace roofing beneath retained metal. Specific Replacement and Repairs: e. Associated roof work: Retain rooftop HVAC units in place and replace roofing beneath elevated units and frames and around curbs. Replace old or deteriorated wooden rooftop support blocks with load-rated black rubber blocks compatible with the roofing; retain serviceable recently replaced blocks. Replace roof-drain covers/strainers and recondition retained drains with watertight connections. Reflash existing scuppers and provide new scuppers only where detailed; retain gutters and downspouts unless otherwise indicated. Correct approximately 250 square feet of depressed roof on the original building's middle section north of the penthouse to provide positive drainage. Replace expansion-joint weatherproofing/cover material at two original-building sections, approximately 40 linear feet each. Temporarily remove and reinstall the existing lightning-protection system in its original locations and configuration with new clips securing it; complete specified testing and certification. Repair approximately 150 linear feet of the existing movable stanchion-andrope warning-line barrier. Replace the penthouse roof-access ladder to meet applicable VA safety requirements and OSHA criteria. Install 3-foot by 3-foot walking pads with 8-inch clear gaps along approximately 600 linear feet of total walkway route, including gaps. Provide positive drainage to roof drains and scuppers throughout all reroofed areas. Standing water shall not remain more than 48 hours after rainfall ends under conditions conducive to drying. Correct low spots and other drainage deficiencies that prevent compliance before final acceptance. f. Skylights: Replace four skylights: two approximately 85 square feet each and two approximately 40 square feet each. Field-verify openings and provide complete watertight installations. Before fabrication, submit contractor shop drawings and supporting structural calculations signed and sealed by a licensed structural engineer responsible for their design/review. g. Submittals, record drawings, and closeout: Provide required construction submittals and complete specified testing, inspections, and closeout. Submit a clean, coordinated as-built record drawing set in searchable PDF and editable CAD showing actual installed conditions and accepted changes; redline markups alone are not acceptable. Provide a 20-year nodollar-limit (NDL) warranty and maintenance information, complete cleanup and restoration, and comply with contract records-management, privacy, and security requirements. In accordance with VAAR 836.204, the estimated magnitude of the resulting construction price range is estimated to be between $2,000,000.00 and $5,000,000.00.
